source: All Gentoo profile package.mask files plus curated recent error guides

no_mask: No package.mask entry in the downloaded database matched this package.
If emerge still calls it masked, check the exact emerge message: it may be a keyword mask, a mask in your local /etc/portage, or a mask added after this database was built.
meaning: Portage is refusing this package on purpose. That is different from a download failure.
steps: 1. Read the mask reason before changing anything.
2. Put the exact atom in /etc/portage/package.unmask if it is hard-masked.
3. Put the exact atom in /etc/portage/package.accept_keywords if emerge says the keyword is missing.
4. Re-run the emerge command and read the next message.
messages.built: Local Portage entries merged; database now has {count} entries at {path}.
messages.missing: No database at {path}. Run: gentoo explain db fetch
messages.guide_missing: No explanation named {name}. Run: gentoo explain guides
messages.lookup_none: No guide or mask entry matched {query}. Try: gentoo explain guides

tips.title: Hard mask vs keyword mask:
tips.body:
A hard mask lives in package.mask and means the distro or your config says no.
  A keyword mask means the package is not marked stable for your architecture.
  They need different fixes, so read the emerge message carefully.

tips.title: Use exact atoms:
tips.body:
Prefer =category/package-version over a bare package name when unmasking.
  That limits the change to one version and makes later undo easy.

tips.title: Before unmasking:
tips.body: Read the mask comment, check USE flags with emerge --verbose, and remember that masks often exist for broken builds or security reasons.

tips.title: Downloaded DB vs local DB:
tips.body: The downloaded database covers Gentoo profile masks. Run `gentoo explain db build` to merge your own /etc/portage entries into the local copy.

tips.title: Offline use:
tips.body: Run `gentoo explain db fetch` once while online. After that every `gentoo explain masked <package>` lookup reads only the local compressed database.

tips.title: Read the whole emerge error:
tips.body: The last line is often only a summary. The useful line is usually the first ERROR or the blocked package list above it.

tips.title: Dry run before changing config:
tips.body:
Use --ask so Portage shows the plan before it changes the system.
  Example: emerge --ask --verbose <package>

tips.title: One change at a time:
tips.body:
Change one mask, keyword, or USE flag, then rerun emerge.
  That makes it obvious which edit fixed or broke things.

tips.title: Keep a config backup:
tips.body:
Copy /etc/portage before a bigger change.
  Example: sudo cp -a /etc/portage /etc/portage.backup

tips.title: Use exact package atoms:
tips.body:
=category/package-version limits the change to one version.
  category/package applies to the whole package and is broader.

tips.title: Mask reason first:
tips.body:
The comment above a mask usually gives a removal date or bug number.
  Read it before overriding the mask.

tips.title: Short forms:
tips.body:
gentoo <package> checks a masked package.
  gentoo <guide> opens a guide.
  gentoo with no arguments lists guides.

tips.title: Save the first real error:
tips.body:
The final emerge summary hides the real cause.
  Keep the first ERROR line, the build.log path, and emerge --info output.

tips.title: Read news before big updates:
tips.body:
Many 2026 reports were solved by news items that required a profile, USE, or config change.
  Run: eselect news read new

tips.title: Sync before deep debugging:
tips.body:
Reports with Unknown snapshot or masked by corruption were often fixed by a clean sync.
  Run: emaint --auto sync

guides.title: Why a package is masked
body: A mask is Portage refusing a package on purpose.
It is different from a missing download or a compile error.
package.mask: a hard mask; the distro or your config says no.
keyword: the version is not marked stable for your architecture.
license: the license is not accepted in your config.
Only override a mask after reading the comment above it.

guides.title: Stable vs testing keywords
body: Portage keywords say how mature a version is for your architecture.
Use the exact atom from the emerge error instead of a broad rule.

guides.title: Unmasking safely
body: Unmasking is not the same as accepting a keyword.
Hard masks live in package.mask; keyword problems live in acceptance files.
Then rerun emerge and read the next message.

guides.title: Blocked packages
body: A blocker means two packages or slots cannot be installed together.
Remove or unmerge the conflicting package.
Change a USE flag that pulled in the conflict.
Install a different slot if both versions are needed.
Read each suggested change before accepting it.

guides.title: Slots
body: A slot lets more than one version of a package stay installed.
The part after a colon is the slot, such as dev-libs/foo:0 or dev-libs/foo:1.
If versions conflict, check whether the target package needs a specific slot.
Do not mask a whole package when only one slot is the problem.

body: Gentoo can refuse a package because its license is not accepted.
Read the emerge error for the exact license name.

Accept a license globally only when you understand what it means.

guides.title: Recent Gentoo errors people hit
body: Common errors from recent 2026 Gentoo reports:
missing-keyword  package.unmask did not fix masked by missing keyword
hard-mask  stable package suddenly masked by package.mask
slot-conflict  two versions pulled into one slot
build-failure  C compiler cannot create executables or toolchain trouble
portage-traceback  emerge crashes with Python traceback
zlib-ng  zlib and zlib-ng soft block each other
corruption-snapshot  masked by corruption or unknown LLVM snapshot
zswap-lowmem  builds hang with high kernel time on low RAM
profile-broken  strange masks after a broken profile symlink
rebuild-cycles  updates that seem to never end
depclean  depclean fails or wants to remove wanted packages

guides.title: masked by missing keyword
body: Symptoms from recent keepassxc and emacs reports:
All ebuilds that could satisfy the atom have been masked.
One package is listed as masked by missing keyword or ~amd64 keyword.
package.unmask only overrides package.mask. It does not accept keywords.
~amd64 means testing is available; ** means the package has no keyword for your arch.

Source: 2026-04 gentoo-user keepassxc thread and Gentoo forum unmasking threads.

guides.title: stable package suddenly hard masked
body: The installed package is listed as masked by package.mask.
emerge reports installed packages are masked.
A maintainer may mask a package for Qt/toolchain breakage, security, removal, or low maintenance.
The mask comment usually names the date and bug.
Use package.unmask only after understanding the reason.
Consider the alternatives named in the mask comment.

guides.title: Multiple package instances in a single slot
body: Multiple package instances within a single package slot have been pulled into the dependency graph.
The conflict names a slot such as sys-auth/polkit-qt:0.
Two packages want different versions or USE sets of the same slot.
A newer revision may drop support for an older Qt/toolchain combination.
Prefer a full world update instead of a single-package upgrade.
Align USE flags, or mask the unwanted version temporarily.
If old software needs the old slot, do not upgrade the conflicting slot by itself.
Source: 2026-01 gentoo-user emerge conflict report involving polkit-qt.

guides.title: Unsatisfied REQUIRED_USE constraints
body: The following REQUIRED_USE flag constraints are unsatisfied.
Examples from reports: boot? ( kernel-install ), llvm_slot_21, rust-analyzer? ( rust-src ).
A selected USE flag requires another flag, slot, or target.
Sometimes a stale profile or old repo makes a valid combination look impossible.
Add the required flag in /etc/portage/package.use/local, or disable the parent flag.
Read the constraint literally: a? ( b ) means if a is on, b must also be on.
Sync the tree and recheck before broad changes.
Source: 2026-04 systemd-utils report and 2026-01 rust LLVM_SLOT report.

guides.title: C compiler cannot create executables
body: Build fails very early with C compiler cannot create executables.
Every package fails during an install, or only one package fails.
Look above the final emerge summary.
Bad CFLAGS, CXXFLAGS, LDFLAGS, or CHOST.
Remove experimental flags and rebuild the toolchain if needed.
Do not reinstall the whole system until the build.log cause is known.
Source: 2026-10 Reddit install report where commenters pointed to flags and build.log.

guides.title: elogind fails to emerge
body: sys-auth/elogind fails during emerge and blocks GUI installation.
Read the build.log and the emerge error line.
Search the reported Gentoo bug number from the error output.
Install the binary package if available, then investigate the build issue later.
Do not blindly unmask or mask unrelated systemd/elogind packages.
Source: 2026-09 Reddit report referencing Gentoo bug 981933.

guides.title: emerge Python traceback after Portage update
body: emerge exits with a Python traceback instead of a normal Portage error.
The traceback mentions load_emerge_config, _sets, or read_configs.
Check syntax in make.conf and package.* files.
If the traceback started after a testing Portage update, return to the last working Portage version.
Correct the config file named in the traceback when it names one.
Report the full traceback if it is a Portage bug.
Source: 2026-08 Reddit report after portage-3.0.82 testing update.

guides.title: Unmatched removal atoms in profile package.mask
body: Atoms begin with a minus sign, such as ->=sys-auth/polkit-124.
A profile mask file is trying to remove a mask from a parent profile.
If the parent no longer has that mask, Portage reports no match.
Sync the repo and make sure the profile symlink is current.
Do not edit files under /var/db/repos/gentoo by hand.
Source: Reddit report about systemd profile package.mask removal atoms.

guides.title: emerge-webrsync fails in chroot
body: PORTAGE_BIN_PATH: parameter null or not set.
mirrorselect or eselect also fail during install.
Check that the chroot environment variables are still set.
Re-enter the chroot and source the profile again.
Try emaint --auto sync once the environment is sane.

guides.title: zlib and zlib-ng soft block each other
body: Binary packages ignored due to non-matching USE.
The update is mid-transition between zlib implementations.
Pending USE changes or unread news can leave the graph inconsistent.
Read news, then do a full world update before emerging the single package again.
Source: 2026-01 Gentoo forum zlib/zlib-ng report resolved by news and world update.

guides.title: Conflicting Python targets
body: Portage asks for python_single_target_python3_12 and python3_11 together.
Packages seem to want different Python versions.
Remove hand-written PYTHON_SINGLE_TARGET and PYTHON_TARGETS pins from make.conf and package.use unless needed.
Let the current profile choose targets.
Sync and retry a full world update.
Source: 2026-02 Gentoo forum Python targets thread.

guides.title: masked by corruption or unknown snapshot
body: ebuild fails in depend phase with Unknown snapshot.
The local repo snapshot is incomplete or inconsistent.
If it persists, check repo config and avoid editing ebuilds by hand.
Source: 2026-02/03 Gentoo forum LLVM OpenMP snapshot report.

guides.title: Builds hang on low-memory systems with zswap
body: Large builds such as GCC or Go use lots of RAM, then sit at high kernel time.
The build never progresses even after long waits.
ps and top while the build runs.
Fix approach reported by a user:
Reduce parallel jobs with MAKEOPTS=-j1 or a low job count.

guides.title: Strange masks after a broken profile symlink
body: Many unrelated REQUIRED_USE, slot, or mask errors after sync.
eselect profile list shows no selected profile.
emerge hints that there is no valid profile.
Select a current profile with eselect profile list and eselect profile set <number>.
If eselect cannot fix it, repair the symlink manually.
Then run a full world update.
Source: 2026-01 gentoo-user report where a stale profile caused cascading errors.

guides.title: Updates that seem to never end
body: Repeated updates keep selecting the same packages.
Finish a normal world update before changing profiles or USE flags broadly.
Run @preserved-rebuild when Portage asks for it.
Source: 2026-10 gentoo-user topics about repeating update cycles.

guides.title: depclean fails or removes wanted packages
body: emerge --depclean errors or proposes removing packages you still use.
Add wanted packages to the world set with emerge --noreplace <package>.
Keep kernel sources and manually managed tools.
Run revdep-rebuild after depclean if libraries were removed.
Source: 2026-10 gentoo-user depclean report and Portage FAQ.
